name: CurbIQ
why: A product line of Arcadis IBI Group, not a standalone vendor.

record.name: CurbIQ
record.description: Curb inventory, regulation digitization and curb management for cities

paragraphs: CurbIQ sells curb management software to cities, universities and airports, giving them one place to keep curb regulations and usage data. The problem it addresses is balancing curb access among pedestrians, parking, deliveries, rideshares and vendors.

The platform pulls curb regulation and usage data from multiple sources into a single database. Records are held in curb data standards including CDS, D-TRO and CurbLR. Map overlays show when and where regulations are in effect, and the tool models what a proposed policy change would do. Data sharing runs through APIs so couriers, ride-hailing companies and navigation platforms can see the current rules.

CurbIQ was founded by Peter Richards, formerly chair of the Institute of Transportation Engineers Parking Standing Committee. The team managed the Southern California Association of Governments Curb Space Management Study. The company belongs to the Open Mobility Foundation, a nonprofit that builds open-source tools for cities. CurbIQ itself is a product of the design firm Arcadis.

name: WeRide
why: Consumer robotaxi operator, not an agency vendor.

record.name: WeRide
record.description: Autonomous robobuses and robotaxis deployed with transit authorities and cities

paragraphs: WeRide develops autonomous driving technology ranging from driver assistance up to fully driverless Level 4 systems. Its footprint now spans more than 60 cities across 13 countries.

The portfolio holds five products: robotaxis, robobuses, robovans, robosweepers and a driver-assistance system. Between them they cover passenger mobility, logistics and street sanitation. The robobus is offered for public operations including day transport, bus rapid transit and night shuttle service. Robotaxi public operations are listed in cities including Guangzhou, Abu Dhabi, Zurich, Dubai and Singapore. The driverless stack runs on a computing platform rated at 2,000 TOPS.

The company was established in 2017 and has run an autonomous vehicle fleet for more than 2,500 days. It is listed on Nasdaq and the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. It states that its products hold autonomous driving permits in eight markets, among them China, the United Arab Emirates, Singapore and France. Named partners include global carmakers, ride-hailing firms and Tier 1 suppliers.
